newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares revel in five-day surge.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares revel in five-day surge.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 2.91 percent on Monday to extend their winning streak to five days in a row.
Traders said the market was driven higher by persistent demand for shares of newly privatised companies and that such demand should keep the upward trend intact over the short term.
"As long as demand for shares of newly privatised companies, especially Lek, remains as high as it is now, shares will continue rising," one trader said.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 29.27 points to 1,036.52.
* 18 shares rose and two fell, while four were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 382.3 million tolars from 396.5 million.
* Lek's issue A was the most actively traded, firming 1.94 percent to 19,039 tolars on volume of 10,970 shares for total turnover of 208.9 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Dadas was the biggest gainer, surging 26.39 percent to 20,189 tolars on volume of 781 shares for total turnover of 15.8 million tolars.

Traders said Dadas' rise was the result of a general belief that its shares have already bottomed out. Shares of Dadas have fallen over 90 percent since March on accusations its brokerage was rigging prices by trading among its affiliated companies.

* Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the leading decliner, tumbling 7.82 percent to 12,207 tolars on volume of 220 shares for total turnover of 2.7 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
